name: Garibaldi Lake Campground
summary: Lakeside tent sites with cooking shelters, pit toilets, and food hangs.
caution: Reservations required year-round; no overnight use of day-use shelters.

name: Taylor Meadows Campground
summary: Meadow tent platforms with day-use shelters and food hangs.
caution: Reservations required year-round; carry out all garbage.

name: Helm Creek Campground
summary: Subalpine platforms beside Helm Creek, with pit toilets and food hangs.
caution: 8.5 km via Cheakamus Lake trailhead; official pages disagree on pad count (9 versus 30).

name: Cheakamus Lake Campground
summary: Forested lake-shore backcountry camping with pit toilets and food hangs.
caution: Reservation listing says 8 reservable pads; area description says 10 cleared sites.

name: Singing Creek Campground
summary: Small, forested campground farther along Cheakamus Lake.
caution: Reservation listing says 6 pads; area description says 7 cleared sites.

name: Russet Lake Campground
summary: High-alpine tent sites at Russet Lake with pit toilets and seasonal food hangs.
caution: Food hangs are removed in winter; BC Parks directs campers to the black storage box instead. Distance/elevation are via Singing Pass from Whistler Village.

name: Elfin Lakes Campground
summary: Ridge-and-lake camping on tent platforms with food hangs and pit toilets.
caution: Separate Elfin Lakes Shelter bunk reservations are not part of this campground record.

name: Wedgemount Lake Campground
summary: Steep alpine approach to two camping areas with 10 pads each.
caution: The lower lakeshore toilet is seasonal; the upper toilet near the emergency hut remains available year-round.

name: Rampart Ponds Campground
summary: Remote platforms with pit toilets and food storage beyond Elfin Lakes.
caution: CLOSED UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE (BC Parks advisory, March 26, 2026): washed-out crossing at Zig Zag Creek; no alternate access route. Do not plan a stay; check current park advisories.

name: Red Heather Campground (winter only)
summary: Winter-only on-snow backcountry camping near Red Heather day-use shelter.
caution: Camping permitted December 1 through April 30 only; overnight use of the day shelter is not allowed.

name: Viewpoint Beach Campground
summary: Hike-in tent pads along West Canyon Trail with pit toilets and a bear cache.
caution: No campfires in Golden Ears hike-in backcountry; dogs must remain under control.

name: Hiker's Beach Campground
summary: Hike-in backcountry beach campsite along West Canyon Trail with bear cache.
caution: BC Parks lists 20 pads and a bear cache at Hiker’s Beach, but does not confirm a toilet at this specific campground. Check current facilities; no campfires in the hike-in backcountry.

name: Alder Flats Campground
summary: Forested tent pads on West Canyon Trail with pit toilets.
caution: BC Parks lists tent pads and toilets but no provided food cache at Alder Flats; plan independent secure food storage.

name: Halfmoon Beach Campground
summary: Riverside or beach-area hike-in camping along East Canyon Trail with pit toilets and bear cache.
caution: No campfires in the hike-in backcountry.

name: Panorama Ridge Campground
summary: High-elevation tent pads beside the Golden Ears Trail, near the emergency shelter.
caution: BC Parks lists tent pads and a urine-diversion toilet but no provided food cache at Panorama Ridge; plan independent secure food storage.

name: East Beach Campground
summary: Reservable boat-access-only camping on the west shore of Alouette Lake with pit toilets.
caution: BOAT-ACCESS ONLY: not a hiking-trail destination. Exclude from hike-only filters.

name: Buckhorn Campground
summary: Heather Trail subalpine meadows with tent pads, outhouses, shelter, and bear cache.
caution: Peak-season reservations required; campfires prohibited.

name: Kicking Horse Campground
summary: Remote Heather Trail meadow campground with outhouse and bear cache.
caution: Peak-season reservations required; campfires prohibited.

name: Frosty Creek Campground
summary: Strenuous Frosty Mountain Trail approach to nine pads and a pit toilet.
caution: BC Parks lists tent pads, a toilet and emergency shelter, but no provided food cache at Frosty Creek; plan independent secure food storage.

name: Upper Joffre Lake Campground
summary: Glacial-lake campground with tent pads, urine-diversion toilet, and bear-proof locker.
caution: Reservations required for the camping season; no pets or campfires. Check Indigenous-led closures and park advisories.

name: Quiniscoe Lake Campground
summary: Thirty tent pads with four pit toilets and food caches near Quiniscoe Lake.
caution: FOOD CACHES ARE NOT BEAR-PROOF. Lake of the Woods and Pyramid Lake campgrounds remain closed following wildfire damage.

name: Magog Lake Campground
summary: Alpine campground with cooking areas, pit toilets, and food storage lockers.
caution: Remote hiking approaches differ significantly; check access and permits for adjacent national parks.

name: Og Lake Campground
summary: Lakeside ten-pad campground with outhouse, food lockers, and cooking area.
caution: About 5 km from Magog Lake; this is not a trailhead-to-campground distance.

name: Porcupine Campground
summary: Backcountry camping near Citadel Pass with pit toilet, kitchen area, and bear caches.
caution: Reservation required in peak season; route length depends on chosen approach.

name: Kinney Lake Campground
summary: Berg Lake Trail campground at Kinney Lake with pit toilet and bear-proof locker.
caution: Overnight dogs are prohibited. Campground is in BC near Jasper, not Jasper National Park.

name: Whitehorn Campground
summary: Berg Lake Trail campground with tent pads, pit toilets, and bear-proof food lockers.
caution: Overnight dogs are prohibited; check trail and bridge advisories.

name: Emperor Falls Campground
summary: Small campground farther along Berg Lake Trail near Emperor Falls.
caution: Overnight dogs are prohibited; reserve during operating peak season.

name: Marmot Campground
summary: Small alpine campground along the Berg Lake Trail with lockers and pit toilets.
caution: Service availability changes outside the operating season.

name: Berg Lake Campground
summary: Twenty-six-pad campground beneath Mount Robson with pit toilets and bear-proof lockers.
caution: Check weather, terrain, and the latest trail reopening advisories.

name: Rearguard Campground
summary: Six-pad campground beyond Berg Lake on the Berg Lake Trail.
caution: Off-season toilets are not maintained and facilities may not be serviced.

name: Robson Pass Campground
summary: High backcountry campground near Robson Pass with food lockers and pit toilets.
caution: Near the provincial boundary; check park and national-park access regulations.

name: Nicomen Lake Campground
summary: A remote alpine-lake campground with a shelter, outhouse, and bear cache.
caution: The lake may remain frozen into early July.

name: Lindeman Lake Campground
summary: Designated lakeside backcountry tenting area reached from the Post Creek trailhead.
caution: Backcountry permit registration required; registering does not reserve a tent pad. BC Parks reported only four usable pads after wind damage in June 2026; verify conditions before travel.

name: Greendrop Lake Campground
summary: Small designated backcountry camping area deeper in the Chilliwack Lake trail system.
caution: Permit registration is not a campsite reservation. BC Parks warns of stormfall and washouts beyond Lindeman Lake; check the current trail advisory.

name: Flora Lake Campground
summary: Remote alpine lake camping on the rugged Flora Lake trail.
caution: No toilet or supplied food cache. BC Parks describes the Greendrop-to-Flora trail as difficult to follow and suitable for experienced route finders.

name: Radium Lake Campground
summary: Backcountry tenting at Radium Lake above the Chilliwack Lake valley.
caution: Permit registration is required and does not reserve a specific campsite. No toilet or provided food cache.

name: Strike Lake Campground
summary: Accessible woodland backcountry campground by Strike Lake on the Lightning Lake chain.
caution: Register for a backcountry permit; this is not an individually reserved campground.

name: Poland Lake Campground
summary: Alpine-lake campground with a shelter, toilets and a bear cache.
caution: The 8 km approach from Strawberry Flats is strenuous; snow can linger into July.

name: Mowich Campground
summary: Small Skyline II Trail camp at approximately 1,600 m.
caution: 12.5 km is from Strawberry Flats. Water can be scarce in dry summers.

name: Pacific Crest Campground
summary: Compact campground on the Pacific Crest Trail near the Frosty Mountain junction.
caution: BC Parks lists tent space, toilet and fire ring, but no provided food cache at Pacific Crest Campground; plan independent secure food storage.

name: Monument 78 Campground
summary: Designated camp just north of the Canada–US border on the Pacific Crest Trail.
caution: BC Parks lists designated tent sites and a toilet, but no provided food cache at Monument 78; plan independent secure food storage.

name: Grainger Creek Campground
summary: Small horse-camp/backcountry site on the Hope Pass Trail near Grainger Creek.
caution: BC Parks lists a pit toilet and firepit, but no provided food cache at Grainger Creek; plan independent secure food storage.

name: Magnesia Meadows Wilderness Camping Area
summary: Preferred wilderness camping area on the Howe Sound Crest Trail with an emergency shelter.
caution: Not a developed campground or a guaranteed tent pad. The sole HSCT rustic pit toilet is here; no food-storage facility is provided.

name: Brunswick Lake Wilderness Camping Area
summary: Preferred wilderness camping area beside Brunswick Lake on the Howe Sound Crest Trail.
caution: Not a developed campground. Emergency shelter is not accommodation; no toilet facilities or bear cache.

name: Deeks Lake Wilderness Camping Area
summary: Preferred wilderness camping area near the north end of the Howe Sound Crest Trail.
caution: 22 km is the south-to-north distance from Cypress Mountain Resort; shorter northern approaches exist. No toilet or food-storage facilities.

name: Hawint / Tenquille Lake Tent Sites
summary: Nine managed alpine tent sites at Hawint/Tenquille Lake near Pemberton.
caution: Operator booking required before arrival. Dogs are prohibited, camping is allowed only in designated sites, and access varies by trailhead.

name: Floe Lake Campground
summary: Alpine lakeside tent pads at the south end of the Rockwall Trail.
caution: Reach from the Floe Lake trailhead; summer snow may persist. Parks Canada has issued wildlife warnings for Rockwall trails; check current bulletins.

name: Numa Creek Campground
summary: Forest backcountry campground on the Rockwall Trail.
caution: Numa Creek access trail closed until further notice in 2026 due to bridge washout. Check alternative approaches and live notices. Parks Canada has issued wildlife warnings for Rockwall trails; check current bulletins.

name: Tumbling Creek Campground
summary: Designated campground beside Tumbling Creek on the Rockwall route.
caution: Distance depends on trailhead/route; check backcountry booking and trail notices. Parks Canada has issued wildlife warnings for Rockwall trails; check current bulletins.

name: Helmet Falls Campground
summary: Backcountry camp near the falls at the north end of the Rockwall route.
caution: 14.2 km from Paint Pots via Helmet Creek Trail. Parks Canada has issued wildlife warnings for Rockwall trails; check current bulletins.

name: Helmet/Ochre Junction Campground
summary: Designated campground at the Helmet Creek/Ochre Creek junction.
caution: 5.8 km from Paint Pots on the Rockwall route; trail conditions vary. Parks Canada has issued wildlife warnings for Rockwall trails; check current bulletins.

name: Lake O’Hara Campground
summary: Highly sought-after backpacking campground with tent pads, outhouses and food lockers.
caution: 11 km refers to the lake access road; booked campers normally use the Parks Canada shuttle. Advance campground reservations are essential.

name: Hermit Meadows Campground
summary: Steep alpine backcountry campground with eight sites and bear-proof storage.
caution: Reservable only during the published summer booking period; short approach is exceptionally steep.

name: Mystic Beach Campground
summary: Beach camping area along the Juan de Fuca Marine Trail.
caution: Backcountry camping permit is required, but it does not reserve a specific site. Camp on beach rather than disturbing the forest; no individually reserved pads.

name: Bear Beach Campground
summary: Coastal backcountry camping area on the Juan de Fuca Marine Trail.
caution: Bear Beach remains accessible via the China Beach end, but the Juan de Fuca section between Bear Beach and Chin Beach is CLOSED due to a slope failure (BC Parks advisory Oct 6, 2026). Do not plan a through-hike.

name: Chin Beach Campground
summary: Remote beach camping area on the Juan de Fuca Marine Trail.
caution: Approach from Sombrio Beach (~8 km one-way via current open side), NOT from China Beach: the Juan de Fuca section between Bear Beach and Chin Beach is CLOSED as of October 6, 2026.

name: Sombrio Beach Campground
summary: Marine Trail beach camp with West Sombrio tent pads.
caution: Backcountry camping permit is required, but it does not reserve a specific site. Use the established West Sombrio tent pads where directed.

name: Little Kuitsche Creek Campground
summary: Forested backcountry campground on the Juan de Fuca Marine Trail.
caution: Backcountry camping permit is required, but it does not reserve a specific site. Use designated tent pads; campfires prohibited.

name: Payzant Creek Campground
summary: Forested backcountry campground on the Juan de Fuca Marine Trail.
caution: Backcountry camping permit is required, but it does not reserve a specific site. Use designated tent pads; no direct shoreline access; campfires prohibited.

name: Circlet Lake Campground
summary: Alpine basecamp on the Forbidden Plateau route toward Mount Albert Edward.
caution: Seasonal backcountry permit registration; permit does not reserve a tent pad. Food cache availability is not confirmed individually. BC Parks has conflicting area-wide campsite counts.

name: Kwai Lake Campground
summary: Designated lakeside camping accessible from the Paradise Meadows trail network.
caution: Seasonal backcountry permit registration; permit does not reserve a tent pad. Food cache availability is not confirmed individually. BC Parks has conflicting area-wide campsite counts.

name: Lake Helen Mackenzie Campground
summary: Designated backcountry camping in the Paradise Meadows area.
caution: Seasonal backcountry permit registration; permit does not reserve a tent pad. Food cache availability is not confirmed individually. BC Parks has conflicting area-wide campsite counts.

name: Bedwell Lake Campground
summary: Designated tenting site along the Bedwell Lakes trail.
caution: Seasonal backcountry permit registration; permit does not reserve a tent pad. Food cache availability is not confirmed individually. BC Parks has conflicting area-wide campsite counts.

name: Baby Bedwell Lake Campground
summary: Smaller designated backcountry campground on the Bedwell Lakes trail.
caution: Seasonal backcountry permit registration; permit does not reserve a tent pad. Food cache availability is not confirmed individually. BC Parks has conflicting area-wide campsite counts.

name: Nels Bight Camping Area
summary: Popular broad sandy-beach wilderness camping area near Cape Scott.
caution: Backcountry camping fee permit is not a tent-pad reservation. Beach wilderness camping; no individually reserved tent pad.

name: Nissen Bight Camping Area
summary: Long coastal camping beach on the Cape Scott and North Coast trail network.
caution: Backcountry camping fee permit is not a tent-pad reservation. Beach wilderness camping; tide awareness required.

name: San Josef Bay Camping Area
summary: Short hike to a sweeping sandy beach with backcountry camping.
caution: Backcountry camping fee permit is not a tent-pad reservation. Beach wilderness camping; camp above high tide.

name: Guise Bay Camping Area
summary: Remote beach camping area in Cape Scott Park.
caution: Backcountry camping fee permit is not a tent-pad reservation. Beach wilderness camping; longer rough approach.

name: Eric Lake Campground
summary: Established forest campground with tent pads near the start of Cape Scott Trail.
caution: Official BC Parks page is inconsistent: Eric Lake lists 11 tent pads in the main trail section but eight in another hiking section. Existing count is 11; confirm current capacity before travel.

name: Fisherman River Campground
summary: Small trail campground beside Fisherman River.
caution: Backcountry camping fee permit is not a tent-pad reservation. Has a pit toilet but explicitly no food cache; secure food independently.

name: Kaslo Lake Campground
summary: Alpine tent-pad campground with a cooking shelter and secure food storage.
caution: BC Parks park overview lists 10 tent pads while its hiking guide lists 8; capacity intentionally left blank pending confirmation. Check access road.

name: Tanal Lake Campground
summary: Small alpine tenting area near Tanal Lake with food cache.
caution: 6.4 km via Enterprise Creek trail, which BC Parks says is no longer regularly maintained.

name: Applebee Dome Campground
summary: High-alpine campground on the rock slabs above Conrad Kain Hut.
caution: Extremely exposed alpine conditions. Permit registration is required, but a tent site is not reserved.

name: Boulder Campground
summary: Designated campground below Conrad Kain Hut in the Bugaboo alpine area.
caution: Steep access, exposed alpine environment, and permit registration required.

name: Lower Elk Lake Campground
summary: Short hike-in campground by Lower Elk Lake with pads, toilet and food cache.
caution: Backcountry permit registration required. One-kilometre approach is from the Elk Lakes parking lot.

name: Abruzzi Lake Campground
summary: Small remote campground in the Cadorna Creek watershed.
caution: BC Parks states no permit or camping fee required. Rough remote access; verify current trail conditions.

name: Garibaldi Lake
summary: Turquoise alpine lake set below glaciers and volcanic peaks, accessible by the Rubble Creek trail.
caution: Garibaldi Park prohibits pets. Backcountry camping requires a separate reservation. Toilets and food hangs are provided at Garibaldi Lake Campground, not generally along the hiking route.

name: Panorama Ridge
summary: High alpine ridge with sweeping views over Garibaldi Lake and the Black Tusk.
caution: Long alpine day with seasonal snow; stay on established routes and check Garibaldi park advisories.

name: Black Tusk Meadows
summary: Alpine meadows below the distinctive Black Tusk volcanic pinnacle.
caution: The upper spire is technical terrain; this listing is for hiking in the meadows, not a summit climb. Toilets and food hangs are at nearby designated Taylor Meadows/Helm Creek campgrounds, not throughout the meadows.

name: Elfin Lakes
summary: Two alpine lakes reached via the Diamond Head area, with established overnight facilities nearby.
caution: Camping requires a reservation; dogs are not permitted in Garibaldi Park. Toilets and designated food storage are at the Elfin Lakes camping area.

name: Cheakamus Lake
summary: Forest-lined glacial lake with a popular low-elevation lakeshore hiking approach.
caution: Check seasonal road and trail access; overnight camping requires a reservation. Toilets and food storage are at the designated Cheakamus Lake campgrounds, not all around the shoreline.

name: Wedgemount Lake
summary: Steep mountain hike to a glacial lake beneath Wedge Mountain.
caution: Very steep alpine access; snow and difficult footing may persist into summer. Toilets and food storage are associated with the designated Wedgemount Lake campgrounds; seasonal facilities vary.

name: Russet Lake
summary: High alpine lake and hiking destination reached from the Singing Pass area.
caution: Long alpine approach with rapidly changing weather; check park camping rules. Toilets and food storage are at Russet Lake Campground; food-hang arrangements change seasonally.

name: Stawamus Chief First Peak
summary: Steep forest-and-granite ascent to a viewpoint above Squamish and Howe Sound.
caution: Chains, ladders and exposed rock can be encountered. Distance and gain are for the park’s First Peak trail.

name: Stawamus Chief Second Peak
summary: Second of the Chief’s granite summits overlooking Howe Sound and Squamish.
caution: Steep trail with exposed granite. The listed distance is one-way from the park trailhead.

name: Brandywine Falls
summary: Forest walk to an established viewpoint above the 70-metre Brandywine Falls.
caution: Stay at designated viewpoints. The canyon and base of the falls are not publicly accessible.

name: Golden Ears Summit
summary: Long and steep mountain hike from West Canyon toward the Golden Ears peaks.
caution: BC Parks describes the route as a demanding mountain climb. Check closures and trail assessments before planning.

name: Alouette Mountain
summary: Strenuous forest and mountain approach above Alouette Lake.
caution: BC Parks describes a long route with mountain terrain; verify trail and storm-damage advisories.

name: Mount Seymour Summit
summary: Mountain trail across Brockton Point and Pump Peaks to views of Vancouver and Indian Arm.
caution: The official distance is one-way in summer conditions; upper mountain terrain is snow-covered in winter.

name: Dog Mountain
summary: Forested walk from the upper Seymour trail system to an overlook above Vancouver and Indian Arm.
caution: Conditions vary seasonally; check access and winter trail policies.

name: Mystery Lake
summary: Short summer trail to a small subalpine lake near the upper mountain parking area.
caution: The official 1.5 km distance is one-way and based on summer conditions.

name: Goldie Lake Loop
summary: Forest loop through a small-lake landscape in the lower upper-mountain trail network.
caution: Approximate summer loop distance from the park trail descriptions.

name: Elsay Lake
summary: Rugged backcountry lake reached on a lengthy route beyond the main Seymour trail.
caution: BC Parks rates this route difficult and recommends it only for experienced, well-equipped backcountry hikers.

name: Lindeman Lake
summary: Popular forested hike to a striking blue-green mountain lake.
caution: The official distance is the return hike from Post Creek parking; check current trail access. Campground facilities at Lindeman Lake include a toilet and food-storage facilities; verify seasonal site availability.

name: Greendrop Lake
summary: Longer forest-and-lake hike past Lindeman Lake to an overnight destination.
caution: Route was altered by washouts near Greendrop Lake. Check current BC Parks advisories.

name: Flora Lake
summary: Subalpine lake approached by a demanding hike in the Chilliwack Lake trail system.
caution: BC Parks reports the return distance from the Post Creek trailhead; check current trail conditions.

name: Radium Lake
summary: Remote lake destination reached from the Chilliwack Lake campground trailhead.
caution: Official distance is return from the campground area; plan for a long hike.

name: Howe Sound Crest Trail
summary: Rugged north-south ridge traverse above Howe Sound with alpine scenery and wilderness camps.
caution: Exposed terrain and seasonal snow; check current trail conditions and backcountry camping regulations.

name: Eagle Bluffs
summary: Popular mountain viewpoint above Howe Sound and the city, reached via the Cypress trail system.
caution: Check park access, trail closures and winter conditions.

name: Hicks Lake Trail
summary: Easy forest trail alongside Hicks Lake near Harrison Hot Springs.
caution: Official park distance is approximate and return.

name: Deer Lake Trail
summary: Short lakeside forest hike in Sasquatch Park.
caution: The maintained trail does not complete a full circuit of the lake.

name: Frosty Mountain
summary: High mountain hike known for alpine larch stands and a summit outlook.
caution: Official distance is one-way from Lightning Lakes; high trails are seasonally snowbound.

name: Heather Trail / Three Brothers Ridge
summary: Open subalpine meadows and ridge scenery on the Heather Trail toward Nicomen Lake.
caution: The 21 km route is one-way to Nicomen Lake, not a short loop. Check access and backcountry rules.

name: Skyline I Trail
summary: Ridgetop trail across alpine terrain with long views of the Cascade Mountains.
caution: Official park distance is one-way; return or loop routes require additional mileage.

name: Skyline II Trail
summary: Remote continuation of the Skyline network toward Silver-Skagit Road.
caution: Remote point-to-point trail with significant downhill travel; verify transport and route conditions.

name: Windy Joe Mountain
summary: Forested mountain hike to a historic fire lookout.
caution: Distance and gain are one-way from Windy Joe–Pacific Crest parking.

name: Beaver Pond Nature Trail
summary: Short, level interpretive walk with wetland bird-watching opportunities.
caution: Park lists approximately 500 metres for the full loop.

name: Lightning Lake
summary: Accessible lake setting with shore trails and summer recreation in Manning Park.
caution: Lake-side trails and winter routes differ; confirm the route and season before planning. Developed facilities exist at designated Lightning Lake day-use/camping areas; facilities vary along the lake.

name: West Coast Trail
summary: Iconic multi-day coastal backpacking route through remote beaches and rainforest.
caution: Reservations and seasonal operating rules apply; this is a rugged wilderness route.

name: Juan de Fuca Marine Trail
summary: Coastal trail between China Beach and Botanical Beach with beach camping options.
caution: As of November 2026, BC Parks lists the Bear Beach–Chin Beach section as CLOSED with no through-route. Check current notices.

name: Botanical Beach
summary: Rocky shoreline and tide pools near Port Renfrew, accessed by forest trails.
caution: View tide pools at appropriate tides and follow shoreline and park advisories.

name: San Josef Bay
summary: Sand beach reached by a relatively short forest approach in northern Vancouver Island.
caution: Official distance is one-way from the Cape Scott trailhead; coastal tides and remote road access matter.

name: Cape Scott Lighthouse Trail
summary: Long coastal forest hike to the lighthouse area at the northwestern tip of Vancouver Island.
caution: The lighthouse and cape lie outside Cape Scott Park on Department of National Defence private property. Do not trespass; check BC Parks for legal access and current trail guidance.

name: Paradise Meadows Loop
summary: Accessible subalpine boardwalk and meadow circuit at the Forbidden Plateau trailhead.
caution: The official 4.2 km route is a return circuit; alpine access is seasonal.

name: Flower Ridge
summary: Steep climb from Buttle Lake to an open alpine ridge with wide mountain views.
caution: The park describes a steep and rough climb; water may be scarce on the ridge.

name: Landslide Lake
summary: Backcountry alpine lake reached from the Elk River hiking corridor.
caution: Camping is not permitted at Landslide Lake; use designated campsites along the access trail.

name: Bedwell Lake
summary: Subalpine lake destination with designated backcountry camping and nearby viewpoints.
caution: Official route distance is one-way; camp only in designated areas. A pit toilet is at Bedwell Lake Campground; BC Parks does not confirm food-cache availability at this particular site.

name: Della Falls
summary: Tall waterfall reached by a long wilderness trail starting at the western end of Great Central Lake.
caution: The trailhead requires boat or canoe transport across Great Central Lake.

name: Lower Myra Falls
summary: Short forest walk to cascades and waterfall viewpoints near Buttle Lake.
caution: Stay at designated viewpoints; rock and water conditions vary.

name: Englishman River Falls
summary: Forest paths and bridges provide waterfall and river-canyon viewpoints near Parksville.
caution: Some upper waterfall trails and viewpoints are CLOSED until further notice due to storm damage (BC Parks advisory, January 12, 2026). Park-wide 3 km of trails is not a single recommended route.

name: Three Sisters Grove
summary: Old-growth Sitka spruce grove accessed from the Carmanah Valley trail network.
caution: The 1.5 km distance begins at the trail junction, not the parking lot; remote industrial-road access.

name: Sunshine Coast Trail
summary: Long-distance trail network through coastal forest, lakes and mountain ridges with shelters.
caution: This is an entire point-to-point trail system; choose and verify an individual section before planning.

name: Skookumchuck Narrows
summary: Forest walk from Egmont to viewpoints over a powerful tidal narrows.
caution: 4 km is one-way to the viewing area. Observe changing tides and remain on land.

name: Mount Steele
summary: Mountain objective within the Tetrahedron network of lakes and wilderness cabins.
caution: Check road access and cabin policies; snow and avalanche terrain occur seasonally.

name: Tetrahedron Cabin Trails
summary: Network of hiking trails connecting rustic mountain huts and lakes above Sechelt.
caution: Overnight stays are restricted to designated rustic cabins on a first-come basis; verify rules.

name: Quiniscoe Lake
summary: Central alpine lake and trail hub for Cathedral Park’s core area.
caution: Reaching the core area involves demanding approach trails or separately arranged access; check wildfire closures. Campground facilities near Quiniscoe Lake include toilets and food caches; food caches are not bear-proof.

name: Lake of the Woods / Pyramid Loop
summary: Short high-alpine loop between Quiniscoe Lake, Lake of the Woods and Pyramid Lake.
caution: The 2 km loop begins in Cathedral Park’s alpine core, not at a road-accessible trailhead.

name: Diamond Trail
summary: Alpine walking circuit around Scout Mountain with open views of the Ashnola corridor.
caution: Alpine-core trail; verify access and seasonal wildfire damage.

name: Stone City and Giant Cleft
summary: Granite formations reached by an alpine trail from the Cathedral Park core.
caution: Park describes these as alpine-core routes; check current closures and terrain conditions.

name: Okanagan Mountain
summary: Rugged dryland trails ascend toward broad views over Okanagan Lake.
caution: Remote exposed trails, variable road access and fire-affected terrain; check conditions.

name: Divide Lake
summary: Interior lake accessible by several Okanagan Mountain trails of varying difficulty.
caution: Route length and difficulty depend on the selected trailhead; verify park access.

name: Myra Canyon Trestles
summary: Historic Kettle Valley Railway rail-trail with trestles, tunnels and Okanagan views.
caution: 12 km refers to the Myra-to-June Springs section, not a round trip; shared-use trail.

name: Spectrum Lake
summary: Forested backcountry lake serving as the starting point for more demanding alpine hikes.
caution: Dogs are prohibited in Monashee Park; access roads may have logging traffic.

name: Big Peters Lake
summary: Remote alpine lake below Mount Fosthall accessed by a steep climb beyond Spectrum Lake.
caution: Difficult alpine trail; dogs are prohibited and weather can change rapidly.

name: Kokanee Lake
summary: Alpine lake in Kokanee Glacier Park reached from the Gibson Lake trailhead.
caution: Camping at Kokanee Lake is prohibited; check seasonal access-road conditions.

name: Gibson Lake Loop
summary: Short trailhead-area loop beside Gibson Lake with mountain views.
caution: Road to the trailhead can be rough; no camping at Gibson Lake.

name: Kaslo Lake
summary: Alpine lake and established backcountry campsite in Kokanee Glacier Park.
caution: Backcountry camping permit registration is required; verify trail access.

name: Silver Spray Cabin Trail
summary: Steep backcountry trail to a remote alpine cabin and historic mining landscape.
caution: Long steep approach; verify cabin availability, access roads and trail conditions.

name: Drinnon Lake
summary: Alpine lake surrounded by the Valhalla Range, with designated wilderness camping facilities.
caution: Dogs are prohibited in most Valhalla backcountry areas; check current trail and wildfire closures.

name: Gimli Ridge
summary: Subalpine ridge beneath the granite walls of Gimli Peak and the Valhalla Range.
caution: This is an alpine hiking area, not a technical climb of Gimli Peak; verify trail access.

name: Cobalt Lake
summary: Alpine lake and views of granite Bugaboo spires from the park access route.
caution: BC Parks notes route-finding in the final section; avoid unmarked glacier traverses.

name: Conrad Kain Hut Trail
summary: Steep access trail to the Alpine Club hut below the Bugaboo spires.
caution: Trail includes exposed steep terrain; hut accommodation requires checking current booking rules.

name: Floe Lake
summary: Alpine lake below a dramatic rock wall in Kootenay National Park.
caution: Check Parks Canada bulletins; backcountry camping and other Rockwall Trail sections have distinct requirements. Facilities are at Floe Lake Campground; backcountry reservations may be required.

name: Stanley Glacier Trail
summary: Trail through recovering forest to an alpine basin beneath Stanley Glacier.
caution: The 4.9 km is one-way for the standard Parks Canada route; guided fossil tours are separate.

name: Marble Canyon
summary: Short walk and bridges over a narrow limestone canyon.
caution: Remain on maintained paths; protected fossil locations are not open to general access.

name: Emerald Lake Shoreline Loop
summary: Walk around Emerald Lake with mountain, glacier and forest scenery.
caution: The official 5.2 km is the lakeshore loop; wet and muddy sections are possible.

name: Emerald Basin Trail
summary: Forested trail beyond Emerald Lake into a mountain amphitheatre.
caution: The park distance is one-way; conditions and trail access change seasonally.

name: Wapta Falls
summary: Forest walk to a powerful waterfall on the Kicking Horse River.
caution: Road access is seasonal and the park advises staying on maintained trails.

name: Lake O’Hara
summary: Protected alpine lake basin with an extensive network of mountain trails.
caution: 11 km is the access road from the Lake O’Hara highway junction, not a lakeshore hike. Seasonal shuttle and campground access require advance reservations; check current Parks Canada information.

name: Iceline Trail
summary: High alpine hiking above the Yoho Valley with glacier and waterfall views.
caution: Exposed alpine environment with variable route options; verify current Parks Canada trail notices.

name: Berg Lake Trail
summary: Major backcountry trail through the Robson River valley to Berg Lake and Mount Robson views.
caution: Main distance is the one-way reconstructed route to Robson Pass, not a return hike or only to Berg Lake (about 19.5 km). BC Parks still links an older map with longer kilometre markers; verify current trail advisories and backcountry bookings.

name: Kinney Lake
summary: Forested hike to a turquoise glacial lake near the start of the Berg Lake Trail.
caution: About 5 km one-way to the south end picnic area, not the entirety of Kinney Lake. Facilities are associated with Kinney Lake Campground on the Berg Lake Trail; check current reopening advisories.

name: Eva Lake
summary: Subalpine lake destination approached from Meadows in the Sky Parkway.
caution: Park describes approximately 6 km one-way; access road is seasonal and overnight camping is regulated.

name: Miller Lake
summary: Alpine lake reached through subalpine meadows from the summit-road area.
caution: Check park road opening and high-elevation snow conditions.

name: Asulkan Trail
summary: Trail into the Asulkan Valley with waterfalls and glacier views.
caution: Parks Canada measures 15.8 km return from the Illecillewaet Valley trailhead to the Asulkan Cabin area; from Illecillewaet Campground, subtract 2 km. Cabin reservations are separate.

name: Balu Pass
summary: Steep mountain hike from Rogers Pass through forest and alpine meadows.
caution: Parks Canada prohibits dogs on this trail. Groups of four or more adults are required July 15–September 30; verify seasonal bridges, wildlife notices, and current trail conditions.

name: Avalanche Crest
summary: Steep alpine hiking trail to a viewpoint above Rogers Pass.
caution: Snow, avalanche terrain and seasonal trail restrictions require current park guidance.

name: Rainbow Range Trail
summary: Route from Highway 20 into the broad volcanic alpine terrain of the Rainbow Range.
caution: Remote trail, limited maintenance and possible fallen trees following wildfire.

name: Octopus Lake Trail
summary: Longer forest-and-lake approach in the Rainbow Range area.
caution: Remote route with seasonal creek crossings and wildfire-related deadfall.

name: Hunlen Falls
summary: Large waterfall and remote wilderness destination in Tweedsmuir Park.
caution: Remote wilderness trail and variable access; check Tweedsmuir park advisories.

name: Trophy Mountain Meadows
summary: Subalpine wildflower meadows and alpine lakes above the Clearwater valley.
caution: Trailhead reached by gravel road; protect fragile alpine vegetation.

name: Helmcken Falls
summary: Major waterfall accessible via established park viewpoints in the Clearwater corridor.
caution: Reduced Helmcken Falls parking during fall 2026 construction; check current BC Parks advisories before travelling.

name: Spahats Creek Falls
summary: Tall waterfall and canyon viewpoint near the southern entrance to Wells Gray Park.
caution: BC Parks posted Spahats Falls parking lot closure for fall 2026 construction. Alternate access from Shaden Viewpoint is approximately 1 km; verify the latest road/parking notice before visiting.

name: Bailey’s Chute
summary: Short river walk to rapids along the Clearwater River.
caution: The 2 km park description covers the short trail; remain at marked river viewpoints.

name: Tow Hill and Blow Hole Boardwalk
summary: Coastal boardwalk and viewpoint trail at the north end of Graham Island.
caution: The full loop is around 2.5 km; respect shoreline conditions and sensitive areas.

name: Cape Fife Trail
summary: Long forest approach to East Beach and a rustic shelter.
caution: Semi-maintained trail and very limited services; hut availability is first come, first served.

name: East Beach Trail
summary: Remote multi-day hike along the eastern coast of Graham Island.
caution: Very remote coast; route planning must account for tides, weather and access. Experienced parties only.

name: Harvey Mountain
summary: Alpine viewpoint above the Bulkley Valley near Smithers.
caution: The official park description lists 5 km one-way and variable seasonal access.

name: Fletcher–Gardner Trail
summary: Long forest trail to the Lower Reiseter Lake area in the Babine Mountains.
caution: Remote trail, commonly used for overnight hiking; check seasonal road conditions.

name: Kinuseo Falls
summary: Large waterfall in the Tumbler Ridge area with short walks from the day-use area.
caution: Kinuseo Falls viewing platform closed for 2026 under BC Parks advisory (February 3, 2026); the upper viewpoints remain accessible. Check whether the platform has reopened before visiting.

name: Monkman Lake Trail
summary: Long wilderness hiking corridor past the Monkman Cascades into the park interior.
caution: Extended backcountry route; verify official information on bridge and trail conditions.

name: Flower Springs Trail
summary: Hike to alpine lakes, flower meadows and waterfalls near the Alaska Highway.
caution: Official park description lists a 5.7 km round-trip route.

name: Summit Peak Trail
summary: Mountain trail from Summit Lake with views into the northern Rockies.
caution: BC Parks advises this route for physically fit hikers; conditions can change quickly.

name: Chuck Creek Trail
summary: Remote maintained trail from Haines Highway into a wild mountain landscape.
caution: Multiple stream crossings and extreme remoteness; check current trail information before planning.

name: Wapiti Lake
summary: Remote backcountry lake approached through the upper Wapiti River valley.
caution: Very remote route; the park gives approximately 19 km one-way to Wapiti Lake with primitive facilities.

name: Muncho Lake
summary: Jade-coloured northern lake surrounded by mountain scenery beside the Alaska Highway.
caution: This is a scenic destination with multiple short walks, not a single measured hiking trail.

name: Munro Lake
summary: Forested mountain lake reached through Burke Mountain area trails above Coquitlam.
caution: BC Parks identifies Munro Trail access via Quarry Road. Trail signs and bridges in the park may be in poor condition; no serviced facilities at this lake are listed.

name: Dennett Lake
summary: Remote lake on Burke Mountain plateau in the Munro–Dennett trail network.
caution: Park trail signage and bridge conditions may be poor. No designated campground, toilet or supplied food cache is documented at the lake.

name: Ted Kay Lake
summary: Small forested lake in the Burke Mountain plateau lake network.
caution: Shown on the BC Parks Burke Mountain area map. Trails may be poorly marked; there are no serviced facilities listed at this lake.

name: Burke Mountain Plateau
summary: Forested ridges, mountain lakes and wilderness scenery above Coquitlam.
caution: BC Parks permits wilderness camping on low-impact established sites but provides no facilities on the plateau. Park trails may be poorly marked and bridges damaged. Campfires are prohibited throughout the park.

name: Widgeon Falls
summary: Waterfall reached from the Widgeon Valley marine-access trail system on Pitt Lake.
caution: BC Parks advises AGAINST the old Widgeon Falls Trail due to unsafe bridges/stairs. Use the signed old road approach where accessible; canoe/kayak access via Widgeon Slough is normally necessary.

name: Widgeon Lake
summary: Remote mountain lake above the Widgeon Valley in the eastern part of Pinecone Burke.
caution: Remote wilderness destination. Park maintenance and trail signage are limited; check route and access conditions. No serviced lake facilities are documented.

name: Widgeon Creek Campground
summary: Marine-access backcountry campground with about ten tent pads, a pit toilet and a bear-proof food cache.
caution: Boat-access backcountry campground via Widgeon Slough (approximately two hours paddling from Grant Narrows). About 10 pads, pit toilets and food cache. First come, first served; no reservation system or permit required.

name: Dark Creek Campground
summary: Marine-access backcountry campground on the west side of Pitt Lake with a pit toilet.
caution: Marine-access campground on Pitt Lake; no advance reservations, permit or camping fees under current BC Parks rules. Facilities are limited and must be checked before travel.
